author: Aaron
text:
Hi everyone,

As I have said at the beginning of my own journal, I am very happy to be here amongst some of the greatest traders I have seen, yet still teach, fantastic.

I began my own journal very scattered focusing on the engulf then the PAZ, but realized I had no structure to my learning; I got a lot of wisdom from Warren’s journal with regards to planning.

So I have decided to spend a month on each ‘price action pattern’ spending 4-6 hours a day loading as many examples as I can on to a PowerPoint file for later revision. I am going to begin focusing on the ‘Flag limits’ I have spent the last few days reading all I can on here from Harry’s article, bravo btw, and Les_Paul’s 1st page as he has a lot on Flag limits there.

I am confused about a point made in the article by If: ‘Signifies the end of momentum’. Ok I understand what the sentence means, but cannot see this on the chart especially with FLs, Let me demonstrate with an example below:

Maybe I am overthinking this as I can recognise DBD RBR zones fairly easily. With signifying the end of momentum, does he mean that momentum is easing not necessarily grinding to a halt?

Thanks all

DT

author: Andyfx
text:
@Daft Trader

Why you say that there is no flag limit because there is no engulf?

Isn't a flag limit simply the upper or lower limit of the consolidation forming the flag, where often price reacts when it comes back because it is a decision point to push price higher or lower (and where supply exceed demand or viceversa)?

What I see in the first rectangle is a drop-base-drop, then the price come back and gets rejected by the lower flag limit of the base, in a lower timeframe we can see that the final drop of dbd enguled the lows of the base.

author: Andyfx
text:
What exactly are we referring to when we speak of the flag limit? Are we referring to the limit of the big flag (if it is a flag) that is broken (so the support or resistance level of the consolidation of the flag), or the limit of the little flag (we can see it on LTF) that often forms where the decision to broke the SR is taken?

Zoom on decision point, there is a little flag of a DBD on LTF.

In this case those 2 decision points that I described are in the same place, but not always, sometimes the FTB occours at the point of the break, sometimes at the place of the origin of the move that broke that SR.
